subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Escapements: The Heartbeat of Clocks
description: A 60-second lesson on Escapements: The Heartbeat of Clocks.

hook.text: Tick, tock — a clock's beat is controlled by a tiny mechanism called an escapement.

buildup.text: The escapement releases the gear train one tooth at a time in even steps.

discovery.text: A pendulum or balance wheel sets the rhythm. The escapement obeys it.

twist.text: Each tick gives the pendulum a tiny push to keep it swinging — energy feedback.

climax.text: The lever escapement in a wristwatch ticks 28,800 times per hour.

punchline.text: Release, catch, release — timekeeping in three moves.

quiz.question: What role does the escapement play in a clock?
options: It releases the gear train one step at a time, controlled by the pendulum
It displays the time on the clock face
